description:
FOUND s495e (the everyday-smoke instrument, task #2099: everyday/modules/Benchmark-Memoize.pl
produced NO output at all under PCL where perl prints "2 bench-obj timestr iters").

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (scratch/s495e/p-evalpkg2.pl; perl 5.40.3 vs main 87e4e4b3):

    my $c = sub { print "ran\n" };
    my $sub = eval 'sub { package main; &$c; }';
    $sub->();

    perl:  ran
    PCL :  Undefined subroutine &main:: called

Probed case by case (the NAME does not matter, the CALL FORM does not matter):
    'sub { package main; &$c; }'                 perl ran   / PCL dies &main::
    'sub { package main; $c->(); }'              perl ran   / PCL dies &main::
    'sub { package Other; &$c; }'                perl ran   / PCL dies &Other::
    'sub { for (1..2) { local $_; &$c; } }'      IDENTICAL  (no package statement)
    'sub { local $_; &$c; }'                     IDENTICAL

So: without a `package` statement the capture works (that is #295, fixed).  WITH one, the
captured lexical resolves to undef and the undef is then taken as a SYMBOLIC sub name, which
is how the empty name `&main::` appears.  Suspect the interaction between the #240 eval-region
`*package*` binding (p-eval-thunk) and the #296-B1 capture-alist lookup: the region rebinding
changes which table the free name is resolved in.  A `package` statement does not affect
LEXICAL scope in perl -- that is the whole point of the reproducer.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE PROBE: core Benchmark's runloop builds exactly this string --
    $subcode = "sub { for (1 .. $n) { local \$_; package $pack; &\$c; } }";
    $subref  = eval $subcode;
(Benchmark.pm lines 692-700) -- so `timeit`, `timethis`, `timethese` and `cmpthese` all die.
Any benchmarking or timing script is dead at its first measurement.

ACCEPTANCE: the five probe lines above all identical to perl, and
`tools/everyday-smoke.pl modules` moves modules/Benchmark-Memoize off DIFF-at-line-1 (it will
then differ on #2084's Memoize item instead -- re-attribute the baseline row, do not delete it).


=== DONE (s501b) ===
Mechanism: the package-switch requalifier (`_binding_at`, the #239 resolver) never consulted the eval CAPTURE list, so in eval mode a `package X;` in the eval text re-homed a captured lexical `$c` to `$X::c` (empty) -- `&$c` then called the empty-named sub.  Fix (Pl/Parser2.pm, ONE resolver): in eval mode `_binding_at` answers 'lex' for any capture-alist name (the #296-B1 rule).  Review round, wider: an IDENTITY-promoted (and span-promoted) file lexical reaches an eval through its global, so it was never IN the capture list and the switch still re-homed it -- such cells now publish their capture pair (`_publish_span_pair`, `_identity_eval_caps`); the thunk binds the SAME box the fall-through found, only the compiler's knowledge changes.
Acceptance: the five probe lines == perl; review r501b-evalpkg == perl except row 9 (`(caller(0))[0]` inside an anon sub is '' -- #233, pre-existing).  Eval cache: the emission depends only on the capture NAMES, which are already the cache key (#296-B1) -- nothing new keys it.  Everyday modules/Benchmark-Memoize now runs (timeit works) and differs on #2084(1) (memoize has no effect) -- row re-attributed by edit.
Guards: Pl/t/eval-capture-01.t pkg_* rows (8 fail on the a0899ba6 code).  corpus-diff 19/111: every differing file = eval capture alists gaining the promoted cells' pairs (+ their forward p-defcell moved earlier in five files).  gate-set-scan 638 files IDENTICAL; sweep TOTAL 18714 (+0) GATE clean.  ir-spec §2b.4 route 2 (normative).
Filed from this member: #2557 (a caller's `our` alias + package switch in eval text), #2558 (pre-existing statement drop, scratch/s501b/m4/brk11.pl).
Bench (s503, quiet box load 0.5-1.2, base a0899ba6 vs tree, interleaved x2 + base control, two full runs -- scratch/s501b/bench-final-{1,2}.log): moo-objs -0.02% (noise); string-eval probe p/evalbench.pl exec +1.29% pooled (run1 +1.99% vs a 2.0% base band, run2 +0.57% vs a 2.5% band) -- FLAGGED as a possible <=1.3% string-eval slow-down, inside the pooled control band.
subject: SILENT-ish CRASH (everyday, core Benchmark): a `package NAME;` statement inside a STRING-EVALED sub makes every captured outer lexical unreachable -- `&$c` / `$c->()` becomes a call to the EMPTY-named sub `&NAME::` and dies "Undefined subroutine &main:: called"; core Benchmark::timeit/timethis is dead because of it
